exposure: Cesarean myomectomy group (EM and SM combined)
SM with fibroid removal before uterine incision suture group
SM with fibroid removal after uterine incision suture group
Timing of fibroid removal (before or after uterine incision suture)
Type of uterine fibroids (III, IV, V)
cohort: 190 pregnant women with uterine myoma undergoing cesarean section
finding: Both endometrial myomectomy and serosal myomectomy are safe and feasible for removing intramural myomas larger than 8 cm during cesarean section, with EM having advantages in shorter operation time and less blood loss, and SM, when performed before suturing the uterine incision, can further shorten the myomectomy time.
mod_finding: This study investigated outcomes of endometrial myomectomy (EM) and serosal myomectomy (SM) for intramural myoma removal during cesarean section, finding EM to have shorter operation times and less bleeding, while SM performed before suturing the uterine incision could shorten myomectomy time.
